provenance.source: Author-defined research brief; not a replication of a published paper.
provenance.method: Prepared offline with the ContextAtlas engine and a separate Python OpenAI adapter. Each actor request receives only its decision facts and randomized option labels/order. Five rounds select two new standalone contexts each after reviewing earlier results; a separate baseline is included. Each X condition has 10 model decisions, organized as five mirrored-order pairs. These are model-generated illustrations, not independent human observations or validated theory boundaries. An early offline transport issue altered typographic punctuation in some planning/reflection inputs. Decision-agent inputs were verified unchanged. Subsequent bridge requests used strict UTF-8 with message-digest verification.

adapter.concurrencyNote: The five studies began in one pool of 12. Two recovery pools of 4 raised the combined limit to 20. Autonomy used one non-actor slot after the original pool drained to one operation, bounding that phase at 10. After legacy processes stopped, two corrected UTF-8 pools of 8 bounded the final phase at 16. Later non-actor operations used 600 seconds. Normal actors retained 180 seconds; the disclosed empty-output recovery used 600 seconds.

provenance.caveat: Offline preparation is not an end-to-end execution or performance test of the published website.

roundOriginSummaries.method: Concise editorial summaries describe the approved prospective planning rationale. The full original rationale remains available separately and unchanged.

interpretationNotes: The response is a stated partner choice. It does not measure contract formation, realized cooperation, or project performance.

The reference vignette describes both firms as qualified and feasible without supplying detailed comparative evaluations. Prior history may therefore change the amount of usable evidence as well as familiarity.
provenance.usageNote: Token usage sums provider-reported usage on recorded responses, including unusable final outputs. Usage for failed or unreturned transport attempts is unknown.

requestAccounting.note: Recorded request envelopes count model operations, including explicit recoveries and any disclosed Codex planning. Provider attempts count returned API responses and documented failures, including bounded retries; Codex operations are separate. Interrupted non-actor operations may include additional sent attempts with unknown cost. Accepted actor decisions are counted separately.

changes.reason: The engine retains equivalent and insufficient-information responses as separate categories. Clarify the limitation of the aggregate focal-selection rate without implying that the recorded categories were conflated. No numerical values or decision records changed.
changes.rawReportRetained: The original model report remains unchanged in the local study.json and calls.jsonl audit.

transportAudit.method: Legacy boundary reconstructed from canonical requests and the observed GBK/surrogateescape configuration; direct Python and corrected UTF-8 requests excluded. This is not a network packet capture.
transportAudit.fix: Strict UTF-8 stdin/stdout and matching Node/Python message SHA-256 checks for subsequent bridge requests.

study.title: Prior collaboration history and partner selection

input.title: Prior collaboration and partner selection
input.x: A documented history of successful collaboration with the focal candidate firm: no prior joint project versus one successfully completed joint project
input.y: Stated preference for selecting the focal candidate firm for a new joint project
input.unit: A procurement manager making one firm-level project-partner selection decision
input.context: A manufacturing company is selecting between two technically qualified firms for a joint process-improvement project. The focal firm and the alternative firm both offer feasible contracts within the available budget. The prior joint project, when present, was completed on time and met its agreed requirements. The focal candidate remains the same firm across the two X conditions. Build a complete reference setting for this decision with comparable current information, and distinguish a stated partner choice from realized cooperation or project performance. This is an author-specified illustrative research question with no supplied paper; any numerical facts in the vignette are explicit modeling assumptions. Keep both partner options feasible and allow a neutral response if the available evidence does not support a preference.

design.title: Prior collaboration history and partner selection
design.researchQuestion: In a simulated X1-versus-X0 contrast for the same procurement manager, decision task, and focal candidate firm, what partner-selection action is recorded when X1 is one successfully completed prior joint project and X0 is no prior joint project?
design.xLabel: A documented history of successful collaboration with the focal candidate firm: no prior joint project versus one successfully completed joint project
design.yLabel: Stated preference for selecting the focal candidate firm for a new joint project
design.unit: A procurement manager making one firm-level project-partner selection decision
design.decisionTask: The procurement manager records a partner choice for the new joint process-improvement project using the same current information for both firms: select the focal candidate firm, select the alternative candidate firm, or record no preference if the evidence is insufficient or the options are equivalent.
design.x0: No prior joint project exists between the manufacturing company and the focal candidate firm.
design.x1: One prior joint project between the manufacturing company and the focal candidate firm was completed on time and met its agreed requirements.
sharedFacts: The manufacturing company needs one external partner for a joint process-improvement project.
The focal candidate firm and the alternative candidate firm both meet the technical qualification requirements.
Both firms offer feasible contracts within the available budget.
The project scope, schedule, and acceptance requirements are the same under either firm's proposal.
The procurement manager has current technical and commercial information for both firms.
design.positiveOption: Select the focal candidate firm for the new joint process-improvement project under the same scope and schedule as the alternative.
design.negativeOption: Select the alternative candidate firm for the new joint process-improvement project under the same scope and schedule as the focal firm.
baselineFacts: The manufacturing company plans one joint process-improvement project with an external firm.
The focal candidate firm and the alternative candidate firm are both technically qualified.
Both proposed contracts are feasible within the approved budget.
The project scope and completion date are identical under either proposal.
The procurement manager reviews current technical and commercial information for both proposals.
assumptions: The X dimension is converted into two levels: X0 means no prior joint project with the focal firm, and X1 means one successfully completed prior joint project with the focal firm; any richer or continuous collaboration history is not represented.
Selecting the focal firm is a narrow stated-choice proxy for Y and does not measure realized cooperation, contract execution, project completion, or project performance.
Both partner options are feasible and comparable, and a neutral response is allowed when the options are equivalent or available information is insufficient.
The scenario details are illustrative modeling assumptions rather than empirical estimates.
sourceNotes: No paper was supplied; the research question is user-defined and illustrative.
Supplied context: the prior joint project, when present, "was completed on time and met its agreed requirements."
Supplied context: the focal firm and the alternative firm both "offer feasible contracts within the available budget."
Supplied context calls for distinguishing "a stated partner choice from realized cooperation or project performance."

report.title: Prior collaboration and partner choice
report.overview:
This vignette asks whether a procurement manager's partner choice differs when the focal candidate has one successfully completed prior joint project (X1) versus none (X0), with both firms otherwise feasible and comparable. The recorded proxy is selection of the focal firm for a new joint process-improvement project; equivalent and insufficient-information responses remain in denominators. At baseline, focal selection was 0.0% under X0 and 100.0% under X1 (+100.0 percentage points). Later contexts often stayed saturated, but competing histories, omitted prior-collaboration fields, and two-sided tradeoffs altered the descriptive contrast.

These model-generated choices concern a narrow decision proxy, not human causal estimates. The contrast is X1 minus X0 in designated-action selection; equivalent and insufficient-information responses remain in the denominators. Repeated and mirrored calls are not independent human participants.

executiveSummary.takeaway: Across executed vignettes, prior successful collaboration descriptively tracked focal selection, but the contrast was highly context-dependent and often boundary-saturated.
patterns: Baseline and several audit, urgency, or co-location contexts recorded 0.0% X0 versus 100.0% X1 focal selection (+100.0 percentage points).
Competing alternative-firm history or a scoring sheet without prior collaboration removed the focal-selection contrast (+0.0 percentage points).
Relevance and tradeoff cues produced intermediate or neutral-heavy patterns, including +90.0, +20.0, and +10.0 percentage points.
executiveSummary.nextStep: Run a balanced follow-up that holds both firms' current terms symmetric while varying only whether each firm's prior project is in the same or a different technical area and business unit; report X0 and X1 focal-selection rates, equivalent versus insufficient-information rates, and mirror agreement.

findings.title: Baseline shows a floor-to-ceiling contrast
findings.text: In baseline, X0 recorded 0/10 focal selections (0.0%) and 10/10 equivalent responses; X1 recorded 10/10 focal selections (100.0%). The descriptive X1 minus X0 contrast was +100.0 percentage points, with 100.0% mirror agreement.

findings.title: Audit and urgency did not attenuate the contrast
findings.text: r1-c1 (public-grant audit) and r1-c2 (48-hour restart) each reproduced 0.0% X0 versus 100.0% X1 focal selection, a +100.0 percentage-point contrast and a 0.0-point change from baseline. Neutral responses were 100.0% at X0 and 0.0% at X1 in both contexts.

findings.title: Competing history displaced focal selection
findings.text: When the alternative firm had three accepted prior projects (r2-c1), both X0 and X1 recorded 0.0% focal selection and 10/10 alternative selections, yielding +0.0 percentage points. In r5-c2, with one comparable alternative-firm project, X0 was 0/10 focal and 10/10 alternative, while X1 was 0/10 focal and 10/10 equivalent.

findings.title: Formal omission and tradeoff produced neutral-heavy outcomes
findings.text: r3-c3, whose scoring sheet lacked a prior-collaboration field, recorded 0.0% focal selection at both X levels with 100.0% equivalent responses (+0.0 percentage points). r4-c1's higher focal price plus longer warranty recorded 0.0% at X0 and 10.0% at X1 (+10.0 percentage points), with insufficient-information responses 9/10 in each condition.

findings.title: Prior-history relevance and site proximity varied
findings.text: A prior focal project in a different technical area (r4-c4) yielded 0.0% X0 and 90.0% X1 focal selection (+90.0 percentage points), while a different business unit and site (r5-c3) yielded 0.0% X0 and 20.0% X1 (+20.0 percentage points). Co-location alone (r2-c4) left the contrast at +100.0 percentage points.

nextStudies: Manipulate prior-project technical relevance symmetrically by giving the focal firm one prior project and randomly assigning it as same-area or different-area while the alternative has a matched record; measure X0/X1 focal selection, equivalent versus insufficient-information rates, and mirror agreement.

Cross a formal scoring sheet with versus without a prior-collaboration field and a price-warranty tradeoff present versus absent, holding price and warranty symmetric when absent. Measure focal-selection rate, insufficient-information rate, and whether the X1-X0 contrast shrinks.

Test a mid-range competing-history ladder in which the alternative firm has zero, one, or three accepted prior projects while the focal firm is at X0 or X1. Measure focal, alternative, equivalent, and insufficient responses plus mirror agreement to locate non-saturated contrasts.
limitations: Most executed contexts were boundary-saturated: with 10 calls per X condition, rates were often 0.0% or 100.0%, limiting discrimination and making small contrasts difficult to interpret.
The focal-selection rate alone groups both neutral categories with other non-focal responses; inspect the separate equivalent and insufficient-information counts to understand non-selection.

The design uses repeated and mirrored model calls on a narrow stated-choice proxy; it does not measure realized cooperation, contract execution, project completion, or project performance, and no supplied paper or human sample validates the patterns.

roundOrigins.summary: The baseline was descriptively saturated, so the selected contexts target different boundary questions rather than repeating routine procurement. r1-c1 varies formal audit and published scoring, while r1-c2 varies temporal urgency after an unplanned stoppage. Both keep the same decision task, X contrast, focal and alternative options, and feasibility conditions while providing independent information about whether the baseline ceiling is context-bound.
roundOrigins.shortSummary: The baseline produced an extreme split between neutral responses and choosing the familiar firm. This round explores whether formal auditing and published scoring, or urgency after an unplanned stoppage, could change that pattern while keeping the partner-selection task and both feasible options unchanged.

roundOrigins.summary: Both prior rounds were saturated at X0 neutral and X1 focal selection. r2-c1 adds a competing alternative-firm collaboration record, which targets the X1 ceiling by making the alternative relationally attractive. r2-c4 adds a focal-firm proximity cue that is constant across X conditions, which targets the X0 floor by giving a reason to select the focal firm even with no prior project. They address different boundary questions while keeping the X contrast, actor, task, and both options feasible.
roundOrigins.shortSummary: Earlier simulations paired no prior history with neutral responses and prior success with focal-firm selection. This round adds either a competing collaboration record for the alternative firm or a proximity advantage for the focal firm, exploring different ways that other evidence might change the contrast.

roundOrigins.summary: These two contexts cover different questions rather than repeating prior saturation tests. r3-c1 adds a current focal-firm commercial advantage that could move X0 off its neutral floor and compress the prior-history contrast. r3-c3 tests a formal evaluation instrument that omits prior collaboration, which could reduce X1 focal selection. Together they probe current-merit movement and procedural suppression while keeping the actor, task, options, and X contrast unchanged.
roundOrigins.shortSummary: To move beyond earlier extreme response patterns, this round examines two different sources of influence: a current commercial advantage for the focal firm and a formal evaluation instrument that omits collaboration history. The aim is to explore current merit and evaluation procedures without changing X or the decision task.

roundOrigins.summary: Select r4-c1 to test a two-sided current commercial tradeoff common to both X levels, which can move choices away from the saturated neutral/focal pattern. Select r4-c4 to test technical relevance of prior collaboration, an unexecuted boundary that may reduce X1 reliance without adding a competing firm record. These cover different questions: current proposal tradeoffs versus domain match of prior success. The other candidates either repeat competing-record or formal-process cues with lower expected discrimination or vary contract form symmetrically.
roundOrigins.shortSummary: This round explores a commercial tradeoff between the current proposals and the technical relevance of earlier collaboration. These questions could reveal whether competing current advantages or a weaker match between past and present work changes the history contrast, while both partner options remain feasible.

roundOrigins.summary: The set covers two distinct questions. r5-c2 tests competition from a single alternative-firm relationship, reducing the extreme three-project alternative from r2-c1. r5-c3 tests whether prior focal collaboration remains diagnostic when it comes from another business unit and site, extending the relevance manipulation in r4-c4. Both preserve the same X0/X1 contrast, keep both options feasible, and avoid exact duplicates of executed facts. Other candidates are retained as controls for symmetric references, formal review, site observation, and disclosure timing.
roundOrigins.shortSummary: One context reduces the alternative firm's competing history from three projects to one, building on an earlier comparison. The other asks whether successful focal collaboration remains informative when it occurred in another business unit and site, extending the previous question about the relevance of past experience.
